lines.trans: You would change your artistic expression for such a shallow reason?
With something like this, we can never surpass our debut hit.
Of course nothing can surpass it! What are you talking about?!
Every single person keeps saying the exact same thing!
That film only happened by chance when dozens and hundreds of miracles piled up!
There's no way anyone could plan a shot like that! Let's do this—roll camera!
Director, I beg you—please take back what you just said.
Everyone gives their best on this shoot. You will do the same.
Let's roll.
It turned out just the way you expected, didn't it?
No, we are shooting today.
Would I not be good enough—in Ms. Kuroki's place?

そんな.gloss: such; that kind of; that much

meanings.note: Before たくさん, means 'that huge an amount'.

examples.text: そんな話は知りません。
examples.trans: I do not know such a story.

examples.text: そんな高いものは買えません。
examples.trans: I cannot buy something that expensive.

meanings.note: Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.
Noun meaning reason or grounds.

examples.text: 遅れた理由を教えてください。
examples.trans: Please tell me the reason you were late.

examples.text: お薦めする理由がもう一つあります。
examples.trans: There is one more reason I recommend it.

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

meanings.note: Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.

examples.text: 俺も金なんとか集めるからよ。もうちょっと明るくやろうや。
examples.trans: I'll scrape together some money too, so let's keep our spirits up.

examples.text: ああ。リスクもあるが、懸けてみるか、トシ。
examples.trans: Yeah. There's risk involved too, though—ready to take the gamble, Toshi?

examples.text: 強制送還の金がかかるだけで、何の見せしめにもならないだろ？
examples.trans: Deporting them just costs money and doesn't serve as an example to anyone, right?

examples.text: あの作品を超えるのはそう簡単じゃありません。
examples.trans: Surpassing that debut film of ours won't be easy.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Refers to facts, matters, or affairs rather than physical objects (もの).

examples.text: 仕事のことを話します。

meanings.note: Colloquial particle, often used to downplay or dismiss.

examples.text: テレビなんか見ていないで勉強しろ。
コーヒーなんかどうですか。
examples.trans: How about some coffee or something?

できる.gloss: be built; open; be able to

meanings.en: come into existence; be completed; can do
meanings.note: With buildings or stores (店ができる), means a new shop has been built or opened.

examples.text: 駅前に新しいカフェができました。
examples.trans: A new café opened in front of the station.

examples.text: 日本語が少しできます。
examples.trans: I can speak a little Japanese.

meanings.note: Polite/dialectal negative ending, especially in ～ません.
Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.
Read なん before だ/です/の, and なに before が/を or alone.

examples.text: 何を買いにきましたか。
examples.trans: What did you come to buy?

meanings.note: Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.
Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

examples.trans: That film only happened by chance when dozens and hundreds of miracles piled up!

examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

examples.text: あんなものはな、何十も何百も奇跡が重なってたまたま撮れただけなんだよ！
examples.trans: That film only happened by chance when dozens and hundreds of miracles piled up!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Limits the preceding noun or phrase to that item alone.

examples.text: これだけお願いします。
あんなもん狙って撮れるわけないだろ！やるぞ、撮るぞ！
examples.trans: There's no way anyone could plan a shot like that! Let's do this—roll camera!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: do for an inferior (tough-guy てやる)
meanings.note: After て-form (勘弁してやる), expresses granting a favor from a position of authority.

examples.trans: I will give you a hand (casual masculine).

meanings.note: With します, forms お願いします ('please'), the standard polite way to request a service or favor.

examples.text: 一つお願いがあります。
examples.trans: I have one favor to ask.

meanings.note: Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

meanings.note: Follows a clause to give a reason or reassuring explanation.

examples.trans: Because it is close, I walk.

meanings.note: Can stand at the head of a sentence without a particle ('right now').
Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).

examples.text: 監督、お願いですから今の取り消してください。
examples.trans: Director, I beg you—please take back what you just said.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Follows a verb's て-form or polite お + stem (お待ちください, お持ち帰りください) to make a polite request.

examples.text: ここに書いてください。

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.

examples.text: 撮影はベストを尽くす、全員。君もそうするんだ。
examples.trans: Everyone gives their best on this shoot. You will do the same.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: ここで働いてるのは全員外国人なんだよ。
examples.trans: Everyone working in this place is a foreign laborer.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Second-person pronoun used by superiors, in songs/books, or between close friends.

examples.text: 君の意見はどうですか。
君ならきっとできるよ。

meanings.en: in that way; that is so
meanings.note: そうですか ('Is that so? / I see') calmly acknowledges news.

examples.text: そうですか、わかりました。

meanings.note: All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.

examples.text: お前ら、観光じゃないんだからしっかりしろよ。
examples.trans: Hey, this isn't sightseeing, so pull yourselves together.

examples.text: 彼女は来るんだろうな？
ちゃんとキャストはそろってるんだろうな？
examples.trans: You've got the whole cast properly lined up, right?

meanings.en: go forward; work out well (いけます = 'it will work!')
meanings.note: Written in kana for figurative headway: いけます! ('this can go / this will work!'), 思いどおりにいかない ('does not go as hoped').

examples.text: この企画ならいけます！
examples.trans: With this plan, it will work!

examples.text: 仕事がうまくいっています。

meanings.en: to think; to feel; to believe
meanings.note: Often follows quotative と to express an opinion or belief.

examples.text: それはいいと思います。

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
Expresses change of state, or in polite customer service (になります) states an arrangement or price total.

examples.trans: That comes to one thousand yen.

meanings.note: Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.
Standard gender-neutral 'I' in polite and business Japanese.

meanings.en: short casual form of じゃあ / では
meanings.note: Brisk spoken transition before taking the next step.
Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.
Attached to surnames, given names, or company names to show everyday respect; never used for oneself.

examples.text: その代わり、今日中に必ず撮りきってください。
examples.trans: In return, make sure you finish shooting everything before the day ends.

examples.text: 全部買ってやる。その代わりあんたの知恵をよこせ。
examples.trans: I will buy all of them. In exchange, give me your strategic brains.

meanings.note: Used in everyday farewells like またね, また明日, and また会いましょう.

examples.text: また明日会いましょう。
